h.strategy: Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the main source of ideas: each hypothesis should exploit a specific open question or a default assumption that may fail under some parent condition. Aim for conditional effects that are non-obvious but mechanistically grounded: diminishing returns when a capacity is already present, substitution between alternative paths, edits that only matter when another part is a bottleneck, and reversals where a normally good edit becomes harmful. Cover a broad spread of edit fields, condition fields and both directions, with no duplicate rationales. State in each 'why' the mechanism and the observable result that would contradict it.

hyps.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 is zero, so a conv on edge 4 (1->3) processes nothing and its gain collapses relative to when edge 0 is live.
Edge 2 (1->2) only carries signal derived from edge 0, so upgrading it yields almost no gain when edge 0 is none.
A skip on edge 4 forwards node 1, which is zero when edge 0 is none, so it adds no signal unlike when node 1 is fed.
Replacing none with skip restores the direct input-to-output shortcut, a larger gain than swapping an existing pool or conv for skip.
A conv sibling into node 3 makes the direct conv_1x1 partly redundant under summation.
Replacing none opens the entire 0->1 chain feeding edges 2 and 4, a larger change than replacing pool or skip.
Adding a conv where edge 5 was none activates a whole path into the output, gaining more than upgrading an existing op on that edge.
A skip bypass on edge 3 already provides a shortcut into node 3, so a cheap conv on edge 5 adds little.
Replacing none with a 3x3 conv creates the direct 0->2 path, a bigger gain than upgrading an existing op on edge 1.
Replacing none with a 3x3 conv adds a new 1->3 path, gaining more than swapping one existing op for conv_3x3.
